fact_label: Five-year foreign-income tax exemption for qualifying new residents
value_raw: Conditional — requires EITHER a USD 150,000 qualifying investment OR Ecuador-source income above USD 2,500/month with social-security contributions, plus SRI registration under this specific regime; runs 5 years from registration, not from arrival
notes: Thinnest-3 backfill (income-viability), 2026-07-18. This is the specific, real mechanism behind the '0% foreign income tax for five years' framing that circulates in expat-relocation marketing — genuinely real, but structurally narrower than a blanket new-resident perk: someone whose only income is foreign passive income (rental, dividends, a pension) and who is NOT making a $150k Ecuador investment does not automatically qualify just by becoming a resident — they would need Ecuador-source income over $2,500/month instead, which many passive-income-only profiles won't have. During the qualifying window, all foreign-source income (dividends, interest, capital gains, royalties, business profits) is exempt; after 5 years, standard worldwide taxation resumes if the 183-day trigger is met. Not independently verified against SRI's own primary text this pass (PDF unreadable, see the primary-source-attempt row).

notes: Thinnest-3 backfill (income-viability), 2026-07-18. Zero-rate bracket runs from $0 to $12,208 (basic deduction, adjusted for CPI inflation from 2025's $11,902 per SRI Resolution NAC-DGERCGC25-00000043, Dec 29 2025); top 37% bracket begins at $109,956. Applies to a tax resident's total taxable income (worldwide, per the sibling fact row above) once any 5-year exemption window has ended or was never claimed.

unit: % flat, withheld at source, Ecuador-source income only
notes: Thinnest-3 backfill (income-viability), 2026-07-18. Relevant for anyone earning Ecuador-source income (e.g. a local rental property) before crossing the 183-day residency threshold, or who never crosses it at all — distinct from the worldwide-income regime that applies once resident.
